F1_riemannHypothesis.text: def RiemannHypothesis : Prop := ∀ (s : ℂ) (_ : riemannZeta s = 0) (_ : ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1)) (_ : s ≠ 1), s.re = 1 / 2

checklist.a_quantifier: every s : ℂ with riemannZeta s = 0
checklist.b_exclusions: exactly the trivial zeros -2(n+1), n ≥ 0 (zeros by riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one), and s = 1 (the pole, a convention value); riemannZeta 0 = -1/2 ≠ 0
checklist.c_function: riemannZeta := hurwitzZetaEven 0 equals Σ n^(-s) for Re s > 1 (zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow; the n+1 form avoids 0^s) and is analytic on ℂ ∖ {1} (analyticOn_riemannZeta), so it is the classical continuation there by the identity theorem

F1_riemannHypothesis.found: Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is the classical statement; the release's RiemannZetaZerosOnLine is the same proposition with the cast written out
F1_riemannHypothesis.second_reading: 2026-11-21, an independent reader from another model family: OK on all four points; adds Mathlib's value at s = 1, (γ − log 4π)/2 ≠ 0 (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Harmonic/ZetaAsymp.lean), so excluding s = 1 removes no zero

found: DirichletCharacter.LFunction: the meromorphic continuation of Σ χ(n) n^(-s) (LFunction_eq_LSeries for Re s > 1; differentiableAt_LFunction off s = 1 for the trivial character; LFunction_modOne_eq: ζ at N = 1)

DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf: every modulus, every character (imprimitive and principal included), Re s > 1/2, χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1 ⇒ L(χ, s) ≠ 0 — for imprimitive χ the extra Euler-factor zeros lie on Re s = 0, so this is zero-freeness right of 1/2 for every primitive L-function
DirichletLZerosOnLine: zeros of every L(χ, ·) in 0 < Re s < 1 lie on Re s = 1/2
PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine: the same for primitive χ (implied by the previous)

'Generalized' = Dirichlet L-functions of every modulus (the usual GRH); the Extended RH (Dedekind zeta) and automorphic L-functions are not stated in the Lean — the remark says ERH is expected 'with more time', so the Lean claims no more than the remark
F2_dirichlet.second_reading: 2026-11-21, the same reader: OK; the character mod 1 is primitive and its LFunction is riemannZeta, so even the primitive statement contains RH; χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1 excludes exactly the principal pole and keeps every non-principal character at s = 1; the three Dirichlet forms are classically equivalent (functional equation for primitive χ; nonvanishing on Re s ≥ 1); the precise label is 'GRH for Dirichlet L-functions' (it implies RH for the Dedekind zeta function of every abelian extension of Q, which factors into Dirichlet L-functions)
